annotations.title: 株式会社インテルゲート｜intelgate,Inc.
InvGate - Build a state-of-the-art IT operation

content.text:
**“IntelGate” can refer to a few different things, depending on context:**

1. **Intelgate, Inc. / 株式会社インテルゲート** — a Japanese IT/web consulting company. Its site says the name combines “Intel” from the Italian word for internet and “gate” as an “entrance,” positioning the company as a gateway for businesses to use the internet. ([intelgate.co.jp](https://intelgate.co.jp/?utm_source=openai))

2. **“Intelgate” as a political-scandal label** — sometimes used to refer to alleged manipulation of U.S. CENTCOM intelligence analysis about the wars in Syria and Iraq, reported around 2015. This usage appears in wiki-style and opinion contexts rather than as a formal official name. ([military-history.fandom.com](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Intelgate?utm_source=openai))

3. **A software/digital solutions company named INTELGATE** — LinkedIn lists an INTELGATE based in Gazimağusa / Famagusta, founded in 2017, offering software, web, mobile, and strategy services. ([cy.linkedin.com](https://cy.linkedin.com/company/intelgate?utm_source=openai))

4. You might also mean **InvGate**, a separate IT service management / IT asset management platform; it commonly appears in searches because the spelling is close. ([invgate.com](https://invgate.com/?utm_source=openai))

If you saw “IntelGate” in a specific article, product, or document, send me the context and I can identify which one it is.
